newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent's gap lower to hit cushion.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent's gap lower to hit cushion.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ An expected opening gap lower in July Brent will bring prices into a strong shelf of support between $18.80 and $17.80, which was its trading range for most of April, chartists said.
+ But Tuesday's sharp sell-off appeared to be a continuation of the drop from early last week that was abbreviated by nearly a week of consolidation. Momentum indicators turn lower.

IPE Brent crude oil, extending its sharp selloff on Tuesday, is expected to gap lower at the open on Wednesday and drag prices into a congestion of support between $18.80 and $17.80, its range from the month of April.
July Brent may also fall below support at $18.88-$18.80, a gap left from early May when prices broke out of that congestion area, technical analysts said.
Brent prices were called 15-20 cents lower from yesterday's close of $18.90, roughly a one-month settlement low.

"We saw a move through $19 and that is quite significant," said Nicola Merrell, technical analyst at MMS International in London. "It should continue going lower towards previous congestion at $18.84-$18.50 but daily momentum is approaching oversold levels so I don't think any move is sustainable."
Brent will remain weak as long as a downtrend line, which crosses on Tuesday at $19.41, is not broken, she said. That line is drawn off the highs of $19.62 on June 2 and $20.35 on May 22.
The $19 level was critical support as it was a Fibonacci 61.8 percent retracement of the rally out of the congestion area in April, Merrell said. She put deeper support at $18.
"The fall from $20.60 on May 16 is still firmly viewed as corrective in nature but it has further to go," said Al Graham at Elliott Wave International in Gainesville, Georgia.
July Brent's 40-day moving average crosses today at $18.84.
"At a minimum we need a meaningful more than a day long corrective bounce and then another new low before this corrective slide from $20.60 wanes," he said in his daily report.
In June gas oil, the break below $173 on Tuesday portends further losses toward $164, Graham said.

"The inability to hold $173 support yesterday opens a direct path to near $167-ish," he said. "This fall from $180.50 is corrective, remains unfinished at Tuesday's low, is supposed to end at not under $164, and should be followed by strong gains to well above $180.50."
